name: News Corp
description: News Corp is a media and information company with four segments. Dow Jones (The Wall Street Journal, Barron's, MarketWatch, Factiva) sells subscriptions and data to consumers and businesses. Digital Real Estate Services is a 62.0 percent stake in Australia's REA Group (realestate.com.au) plus an 80 percent stake in Move (Realtor.com) in the US, and earns the biggest slice of segment profit from listings paid by real estate agents. HarperCollins is the second largest consumer book publisher in the world, and News Media covers newspapers in Australia and the UK, the New York Post and radio. FY2026 revenue was $9.0B (+7 percent).

gics.note: Conventional filing: GICS sector and sub-industry as listed on Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies' (read 2026-10-01; NWSA and NWS both listed under News Corp); the list does not show the industry group or industry. SEC SIC code 2711 (Newspapers) per EDGAR. Digital real estate (REA Group, Realtor.com) is the largest profit segment, which the 'Publishing' label does not capture.

hq.note: New York, NY per EDGAR business address and Wikipedia S&P 500 list

employees.note: About 21,700 employees: about 7,900 in the US, 3,900 in the UK, 5,600 in Australia. FY2026 10-K

businessLines.name: Dow Jones
businessLines.how: Consumers and enterprises pay recurring subscriptions (WSJ had 4,827 thousand total subscriptions, 4,465 thousand digital-only); professional-information customers pay for data and tools; advertisers and event sponsors pay for reach.
businessLines.description: The Wall Street Journal, Barron's, MarketWatch, Investor's Business Daily, Dow Jones Newswires, Factiva and risk and compliance, energy and other professional information products.

operatingProfit.note: Segment EBITDA (non-GAAP); share of total $1,627M including Other -$203M (computed).

businessLines.name: Digital Real Estate Services (REA Group and Move/Realtor.com)
businessLines.how: Real estate agents and developers pay per listing and for premium placement and monthly advertising subscriptions on the property sites; REA also earns from financial services and Move from advertising and related services.
businessLines.description: 62.0 percent of REA Group (ASX: REA; realestate.com.au, realcommercial.com.au, Flatmates, property.com.au) and 80 percent of Move (Realtor.com, under a perpetual licence from the National Association of Realtors); REA Group holds the other 20 percent of Move.

revenue.note: Realestate.com.au had 146.4 million average monthly visits and 12.7 million monthly visitors, 3.5 times the visits of its nearest competitor (Ipsos iris, FY2026).

businessLines.revenueNote: Realestate.com.au had 146.4 million average monthly visits and 12.7 million monthly visitors, 3.5 times the visits of its nearest competitor (Ipsos iris, FY2026).

operatingProfit.note: Segment EBITDA (non-GAAP). Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests was $170M, largely REA minorities.

businessLines.name: Book Publishing (HarperCollins)
businessLines.how: Sells and licenses print and digital books to booksellers, wholesale clubs, technology companies and others (Amazon, Apple, Barnes & Noble, Tesco named); revenue depends on the release schedule and bestsellers, plus backlist titles by authors such as Tolkien and Agatha Christie.
businessLines.description: Consumer books in 15 countries; 120-plus imprints; about 150,000 digital publications; digital 23 percent of global consumer revenue.

revenue.note: 10-K: second largest consumer book publisher in the world by global revenue

businessLines.revenueNote: 10-K: second largest consumer book publisher in the world by global revenue

businessLines.name: News Media
businessLines.how: Digital and print subscriptions (News Corp Australia had about 981,000 digital closing subscribers), newsstand sales and advertising.
businessLines.description: News Corp Australia, News UK, the New York Post, talkSPORT and other UK radio, and the Australian News Channel.

geography.method: Regional revenue tagged in the filing's own XBRL instance: full-year contexts with one geographic dimension (or segments named after places), alone or crossed only with operating segments or a revenue line of the income statement; regions must add up to the revenue line within 1 percent; a member equal to the sum of others is a subtotal; the main split is the largest set of members adding up to the total; anything not broken out is a computed remainder.
